items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to creating the rural
suicide prevention council
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7920

SPONSOR: VALESKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to creating the
rural suicide prevention council

 
PURPOSE:

To establish a Rural Suicide Prevention Council within the Office of
Mental Health to examine and offer recommendations for the prevention of
suicide in rural New York.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

§ 1 - Creates a new section 41.58 of the Mental Hygiene Law entitled
"Rural Suicide Prevention Council"

This bill establishes the "Rural Suicide Prevention Council" with nine
members as follows:

- Two members appointed by the Commissioner of the Office of Mental
Hygiene;

-One member appointed by the Commissioner of Health;

-Two members appointed by the Speaker of the Assembly; - Two members
appointed by the Temporary President of the Senate;

-One member appointed by the Minority Leader of the Assembly; and

-One member appointed by the Minority Leader of the Senate.

The Commissioner of the Office of Mental Hygiene shall appoint the chair
of the council. The appropriate appointing authority shall fill vacan-
cies in the membership of the council.

Membership on the council may include but is not limited to, represen-
tatives of local mental hygiene directors, psychiatric and psychological
practitioners , substance abuse professionals, persons with expertise in
public health, persons with expertise in behavioral health, and others
whose professional expertise includes rural affairs related to the
duties of the council.

The council will be charged with examining the causes and conditions
related to the rise of rural suicide including economics, finances,
housing instability, social isolation, loneliness, alcohol and substance
abuse, and access to mental health care.

The council must also identify policies, practices, resources, services
and potential legislation that may result in the reduction of rural
suicide and rural suicide attempts.

The council must offer recommendations for the coordination of services
and resources among agencies involved in suicide prevention.

The council will create a plan to strengthen economic supports, increase
access to and delivery of suicide care, the promotion of social
connections, the identification of persons at-risk for suicide, and the
use of innovative interventions strategies.

The council shall meet at least two times annually. Members of the coun-
cil shall not receive compensation but will be reimbursed for their
actual expenses.

The council shall prepare and submit a report no later than January 1,
2020 and deliver such report to the Governor and the Legislature. The
report shall recommend policies, legislation, and funding needed to
implement the findings of the council.

§ 2 - This act shall take effect on the 90th day.

 
EXISTING LAW:

This is a new section of law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2017, the Centers for Disease Control released data from 2001-2015
which showed that rural counties had higher rates of suicide than metro-
politan counties. Presently, suicide is the tenth leading cause of death
among Americans with over half a million suicides occurring during the
survey period.

The rise in suicide rates is not attributable to one factor but instead
to a number of factors. Increasing rural suicide may be the result of
economic insecurity, social isolation, a dearth of mental health profes-
sionals, higher levels of alcohol and substance abuse, weakened social
supports, and many other factors.

The Rural Suicide Prevention Council envisioned in this legislation
would be tasked with examining the epidemic of suicide in rural New York
and then creating a comprehensive plan to address the problem.  The
outcome of such a plan would be the reduction of suicide in rural New
York.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
90th day

AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to creating the rural

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7920B

SPONSOR: VALESKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to creating the
rural suicide prevention council

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to reduce the growing rate of suicide in
rural New York through the establishment of a rural suicide prevention
council.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

A new section 7.48 is added to the mental hygiene law entitled "rural
suicide prevention council."

The new council will consist of twelve members to be appointed as
follows:

*Two members appointed by the Commissioner of the Office of Mental
Hygiene;

*Two members appointed by the Commissioner of Health;

*Two members shall be appointed by the Commissioner of Agriculture and
Markets;

*Two members appointed by the Speaker of the Assembly;

*Two members appointed by the Temporary President of the Senate;

*One member appointed by the Minority Leader of the Assembly; and

*One member appointed by the Minority Leader of the Senate.

The Commissioner of the Office of Mental Hygiene will appoint the chair
of the council.

Membership on the council may include representatives of local mental
hygiene directors, psychiatric and psychological practitioners,
substance abuse professionals, persons with expertise in public health
issues, any group, association, or university with expertise in finan-
cial or economic analysis, business planning, and providing supports for
farmers and other individuals residing in a rural area, and others whose
professional expertise includes rural affairs related to the duties of
the council.

The council will examine the causes and conditions related to the rise
of rural suicide, as well as access to mental health care in areas
considered "rural" as defined in section 481 of the executive law.  The
council will identify policies, practices, resources, services and
potential legislation that may result in the reduction of rural suicide
and offer recommendations for coordination of the relevant services and
resources.


The council will create a plan to identify persons at-risk for suicide,
particularly within certain professions, including farming and agricul-
tural work, and to increase access to and delivery of suicide care.

The council shall meet at least two times annually. Members of the coun-
cil shall not receive compensation but will be reimbursed for their
actual expenses.

The council will submit a report by January 1, 2020 to the Governor and
the Legislature. The report will recommend policies, legislation, and
funding needed to implement their findings.

*The amendment to this bill adds two appointments by the commissioner of
the Department of Agriculture and Markets and incorporates reference to
membership by those with expertise in financial or economic analysis,
business planning, and providing supports for farmers and other individ-
uals residing in rural areas.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2017, the Centers for Disease Control released data from 2001-2015
which showed that rural counties had higher rates of suicide than metro-
politan counties. Presently, suicide is the tenth leading cause of death
among Americans with over half a million suicides occurring during the
survey period.

The rise in suicide rates is not attributable to one factor but instead
to a number of factors. Increasing rural suicide may be the result of
economic insecurity, social isolation, a dearth of mental health profes-
sionals, higher levels of alcohol and substance abuse, weakened social
supports, and many other factors.

The Rural Suicide Prevention Council envisioned in this legislation
would be tasked with examining the epidemic of suicide in rural New York
and then creating a comprehensive plan to address the problem.  Address-
ing the root problems of the mental health crisis in our state is a
critical first step to helping the state provide needed services to our
residents.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
90 days after enactment

summary: Creates the rural suicide prevention council; requires biennial reports on the findings of the council.
